text: Few people ever experience life on board an offshore vessel.
Its systems work out of sight, below the waterline and behind the bridge door.
Offshore, a vessel holds its station metres from a platform, with every system on board working as one.
From the bridge to the seabed, each one has to be understood, operated, and trusted.
Not everyone can step on board.
So we bring the vessel to you.
An exclusive Sinor Marine initiative.
A virtual, digital representation of the systems on board, built to introduce, educate, and inform.

title: Vessel Systems Simulator
subtitle: A complete DP2 offshore support vessel, in any web browser
text: Introducing the Sinor Marine Vessel Systems Simulator.
Every system on board, ready to explore.

title: See inside the vessel
subtitle: Realistic · Blueprint · X-ray
text: Change the view in a click.
Realistic daylight, blueprint, or X-ray, to reveal the equipment hidden inside the hull.

title: Learn every system
subtitle: Operate · How it works · Specifications
text: Open the guide, pick any system, and the camera flies straight to it.
Operate it as the crew would, see how it works, step by step, and check every specification.

title: Bow Tunnel Thruster
subtitle: 800 kW controllable pitch · Z-Thrust control

text.say: The eight hundred kilowatt bow thruster turns at a constant three hundred R P M.
text.show: The 800 kW bow thruster turns at a constant 300 rpm.

text: Thrust comes from blade pitch, so it reverses its push without ever stopping the motor.
Explode the assembly, and look inside.

title: Dynamic Positioning
subtitle: DP2 station keeping with live redundancy
text: Dynamic positioning holds position and heading with the thrusters alone.
Hand the bow thruster to DP, fail a controller, and watch the DP2 vessel stay on station.

title: Hydroacoustic Position Reference
subtitle: Type 7950 deployment machine · HPT 5000 transceiver

text.say: The Type seventy-nine fifty machine lowers the H P T five thousand transceiver through the hull, about three metres below the keel.
text.show: The Type 7950 machine lowers the HPT 5000 transceiver through the hull, about 3 m below the keel.

text: From there, it ranges acoustically to a transponder on the seabed.

title: Radar and Laser References
subtitle: RadaScan View · CyScan AS

text.say: RadaScan View and CyScan A.S. measure range and bearing to the platform itself.
text.show: RadaScan View and CyScan AS measure range and bearing to the platform itself.

text: When fog blocks the laser, the radar keeps on tracking.

title: Satellite and Taut Wire
subtitle: Dual Fugro Seastar 9410 · SMT Taut Wire

text.say: Dual Foogro Seastar receivers give satellite positions to about ten centimetres, while the taut wire lowers its four hundred kilogram weight to the seabed.
text.show: Dual Fugro Seastar receivers give satellite positions to about 10 cm, while the taut wire lowers its 400 kg weight to the seabed.

title: SPRINT-Nav DP
subtitle: Inertial and Doppler reference on the over-the-side pole
text: On its over-the-side pole, SPRINT-Nav DP combines inertial sensors with a Doppler log, and keeps navigating independent of satellites.

title: One DP, every reference
subtitle: Weighting, voting and automatic rejection
text: The DP system weighs every reference together, and rejects any one that starts to drift, just as it would at sea.

title: Understand the systems. Work more efficiently.
subtitle: An exclusive Sinor Marine initiative
text: When people understand the systems, they operate them better, and the whole vessel works more efficiently.
